financials_interim.notes: Licensed finance company (leasing/lending), not a conventional trading company -- schema fields adapted accordingly. revenue = Total Operating Income (net interest income + net fee income + other operating income, Rs.446.78mn), the standard 'top line' concept for a financial institution, not gross interest income (Rs.842.62mn, which nets against interest expense). cost_of_sales/gross_profit not applicable (no COGS concept) -- left blank rather than forced. operating_profit = 'Operating Profit before Value Added Tax on Financial Services (VAT on FS)' (Rs.89.50mn), i.e. after staff costs/depreciation/other opex but before the two financial-sector-specific levies (VAT on FS and SSCL) that sit between operating_profit and profit_before_tax in this company's own presentation. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables left blank -- this filing uses a liquidity-ordered (not current/non-current split) balance sheet typical of financial institutions, and the loan book ('Financial Assets at Amortised Cost - Loans and Advances to Customers', Rs.15.91bn) is the core earning asset, not a trade receivable in the conventional sense. short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings deliberately left blank: the filing discloses funding sources (Due to Banks Rs.5.02bn, Due to Other Customers/deposits Rs.8.34bn, Other Borrowed Funds Rs.1.92bn) without a current/non-current maturity split, and 'Due to Other Customers' is deposit funding, not debt in the trade-borrowings sense -- forcing a split would misrepresent the funding structure. EPS 0.008 = 26,857,544 / 3,178,485,367 shares confirmed, no extraction issues found. Cash flow (p.6) is genuinely quarter-isolated in this filing, unlike some other companies this round.

interim_updates.note_text: UB Finance posted Total Operating Income of Rs.446.78mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 42% YoY, with net interest income up 36% (Rs.278.75mn to Rs.379.78mn) on a loan book that grew from Rs.12.85bn to Rs.19.32bn in segment assets (roughly +50% YoY). PAT rose 245% (Rs.7.78mn to Rs.26.86mn). However, the company's own disclosed performance ratios show a more nuanced picture: Return on Assets (PBT) fell from 1.8% to 0.2%, and Return on Equity (PAT) fell from 1.0% to 0.8%, despite the large percentage profit growth -- the balance sheet grew even faster than profit, diluting returns. Segment results also diverge sharply: Leasing segment PBT more than doubled (Rs.38.76mn to Rs.82.00mn), while Loans & Advances segment PBT fell 54% (Rs.35.14mn to Rs.16.01mn) -- the Group-level profit growth is entirely a Leasing-segment story, not broad-based. Impairment charges on loans and advances also rose 114% YoY (Rs.25.92mn to Rs.55.47mn), a credit-quality item worth watching given the Loans & Advances segment's simultaneous profit decline.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one (e.g. 31 March 2026) has been collected for UBF -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Balance sheet fields (current_assets/current_liabilities/trade_receivables/short-and-long-term borrowings) are deliberately left blank rather than forced onto a schema built for conventional trading companies -- see the financial_statements notes for this period for the full explanation of why a financial institution's balance sheet doesn't map cleanly onto those fields.
interim_updates.takeaway: The headline PAT growth (+245%) is real but should be read alongside two cautions from the company's own disclosures: return ratios (ROA, ROE) actually declined because balance sheet growth outpaced profit growth, and the segment breakdown shows the improvement is concentrated in Leasing while Loans & Advances profit fell 54% alongside a near-doubling of loan impairment charges.
operational_highlights: Total Operating Income Rs.446.78mn, up 42% YoY; net interest income Rs.379.78mn, up 36% YoY
PAT Rs.26.86mn, up 245% YoY (Rs.7.78mn a year earlier); PBT up 83% (Rs.26.40mn to Rs.48.23mn)
Despite the profit growth, Return on Assets (PBT) fell from 1.8% to 0.2% and Return on Equity (PAT) fell from 1.0% to 0.8% -- balance sheet growth (assets +50% YoY) outpaced profit growth
Segment split: Leasing PBT more than doubled (Rs.38.76mn to Rs.82.00mn); Loans & Advances PBT fell 54% (Rs.35.14mn to Rs.16.01mn); Others segment loss narrowed (-Rs.16.90mn to -Rs.8.51mn)
Impairment charge on loans and advances rose 114% YoY (Rs.25.92mn to Rs.55.47mn)
Capital adequacy remains comfortable but declined YoY: Core Capital/Total Capital to RWA 20.1% (vs 26.8% a year earlier), both well above the 8.5%/12.5% regulatory minimums
key_drivers: The entire Group PBT improvement is concentrated in the Leasing segment (Rs.38.76mn to Rs.82.00mn, +112%) -- the Loans & Advances segment moved the opposite direction (Rs.35.14mn to Rs.16.01mn, -54%), so this is not a broad-based improvement across the business

Rapid balance sheet growth (segment assets roughly +50% YoY to Rs.19.32bn) is diluting return ratios even as absolute profit grows sharply -- ROA (PBT) fell from 1.8% to 0.2% and ROE (PAT) fell from 1.0% to 0.8% per the company's own disclosed performance indicators

Loan impairment charges more than doubled YoY (+114%) in the same period the Loans & Advances segment's profitability fell -- worth monitoring as a potential credit-quality signal, though this filing gives no further qualitative detail on the cause
